rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 8 compounds if possible and map the elution window without risking severe truncation. This run should show whether retention is compressed, excessively late, or whether the useful phi range can be narrowed in later injections.

All compounds eluted before 10 min, so the main issue is the unresolved 4/5 pair rather than speed. Doubling tG at the same phi window and temperature tests whether that pair is slope-responsive; if R barely improves, later injections should focus on temperature or a narrower phi window instead.

The critical pair is strongly slope-responsive: tG 40 fully resolved it but was too slow, so now move back toward the shortest gradient likely to keep all pairs above 1.5. A 24 min gradient should test whether we can retain full resolution while keeping t_last near or below 10 min.

The threshold for full resolution lies between 24 and 40 min, so bracket it more efficiently at 28 min. If the 4/5 pair reaches at least 1.5 here, we can then optimize speed with temperature or a narrower window; if not, we know we need still more slope relief or selectivity change.

28 min improved the 4/5 pair but also exposed 6/7 as the new limiting pair, so try 32 min to see if both critical pairs can clear 1.5 before paying the full time penalty of 40 min. This narrows the minimum tG needed for complete resolution at the current phi window.

The limiting pairs are not behaving monotonically with slope, suggesting selectivity changes and likely reordering; temperature is the next lever. Lowering to 25 C at the fast 20 min scout should test whether the troublesome pair separations improve enough to beat the current best without incurring a time penalty.

25 C nearly solved the problem with only a slight time penalty, so test a small temperature increase to keep the beneficial selectivity while pulling t_last closer to 10 min. This should show whether there is a temperature sweet spot between 25 and 40 C that gives full resolution with a better overall CRF.

At 25 C only one pair is slightly short of baseline resolution, so a modest increase in gradient time is the most direct way to push that pair over 1.5. Using 22 min instead of a larger jump preserves a strong chance of keeping t_last close to 10 min and improving on the current best CRF.

The peaks elute within a relatively narrow effective solvent range, so trimming the gradient window should keep selectivity while reducing time spent at unnecessarily extreme composition. This narrower window at the successful 20 min, 25 C condition may preserve or improve the critical separation and pull t_last back toward 10 min.

Use the best-selectivity temperature found so far and shorten the gradient one step to try to bring t_last under 10 min while checking whether the near-critical pair remains acceptable. If the key pair stays near or above 1.5, this could beat the current best CRF by reducing the time penalty.

The best run is very close, so now trim only the high-end of the gradient slightly while keeping the successful 20 min, 25 C selectivity conditions. This may maintain the near-critical 3/4 separation but reduce overall retention enough to cut the small time penalty and improve CRF.

The critical pair changes sharply with temperature, and 25 C and 30 C sit on opposite sides of a selectivity crossover. Testing 35 C maps that temperature dependence further and may reveal another favorable selectivity region with lower retention than 25 C.

The temperature dependence is clearly nonmonotonic, so probe the other side of 40 C to map whether a different selectivity region appears beyond that crossover. This checks for a second useful temperature window while keeping the fast scouting gradient unchanged.

At 45 C the run is comfortably under 10 min but two pairs are only slightly under 1.5, so a small increase in tG could achieve full resolution with a modest time cost. This is a good chance to surpass the 25 C result if both borderline pairs respond to slope.

At 25 C the full 0.95 upper bound appears unnecessarily strong and may be compressing late peaks; lowering phi1 slightly could re-expand the late region while keeping all compounds in the gradient. This targets a better balance between the near-critical 3/4 pair and the overall run time around the current best condition.

The only route likely to beat the current best is finding a different temperature-selectivity regime with all pairs near or above 1.5 and t_last under 10 min. Since 45 C was promising but still slightly short on two pairs, test 50 C to see whether one of those crossings improves further.

The severe collapse at 50 C suggests a sharp temperature-driven reordering region, and one more point at 55 C will define whether selectivity recovers beyond it or continues to worsen. With 9 injections left, this is the last efficient check for an alternative high-temperature optimum before focusing solely on local optimization around 25 C.

55 C brought t_last well below 10 min and left only one pair moderately under-resolved, so 60 C is worth one final high-temperature probe to see whether that pair improves while preserving the speed advantage. If not, we can spend the remaining injections refining only around the 25 C optimum.

At 60 C only one pair remains below 1.5 and the run has ample time margin, so the most promising move is a small increase in tG to improve that local separation while likely keeping t_last under 10 min. If pair 5/6 clears 1.5, this should deliver a CRF of 1.0.

At 60 C the limiting 5/6 pair behaves badly with longer tG, so slope is not the right lever; try a slightly narrower high-end window instead to alter selectivity while retaining the excellent sub-10 min elution. Lowering phi1 modestly may re-expand the late-eluting region and improve the only subcritical pair.

Since changing tG and phi1 at 60 C did not fix the 5/6 pair, probe the low-end composition instead to shift where the middle cluster experiences the gradient. Raising phi0 slightly may alter relative compression around the troublesome pair while keeping all peaks well within a fast sub-10 min run.

Raising phi0 to 0.10 gave the best result yet and specifically improved the limiting 5/6 pair while keeping the run very fast, so push one more step in the same direction. This may lift that last pair above 1.5 and reach the maximum CRF without risking a time penalty.

The best condition came from raising phi0, but pushing phi0 further shifted the bottleneck earlier; now trim phi1 one step while keeping phi0 at the successful 0.10. This should probe whether a slightly narrower window can improve the remaining 5/6 selectivity without sacrificing the strong overall speed.

The best run already has ample time margin, and changing the phi window shifted selectivity in useful ways; now test a slightly steeper gradient at the best phi/T point to see if the limiting 5/6 pair unexpectedly improves, as several pairs have shown nonmonotonic slope behavior in this system. Even if not better, this final local probe around the optimum is more informative than revisiting poorer regions.

The 18 min run improved the previously limiting pair pattern and still has substantial time margin, so the final shot should continue one step steeper at the same successful phi window and temperature. Given the nonmonotonic slope behavior already observed, 16 min has a real chance to lift the early borderline pairs above 1.5 while keeping all compounds well before 10 min.
